newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai B shares end up on speculative buying.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai B shares end up on speculative buying.

text.p: Shanghai B shares ended up on Monday due to a flurry of speculative buying in the last minutes after the market spent most of the session down in dull trading, brokers said.
The index edged up 0.017 points or 0.03 percent to 49.084 points on volume of 4.0 million shares worth $1.5 million. Of 41 B shares, 29 traded, with seven up, 11 flat and 11 down.
Brokers said that speculative buying had helped support the market in several recent sessions, but that market sentiment remained gloomy.

"Obviously some domestic institutions wanted to make the technical charts seem good to attract follow-up buying," one broker said. "But everyone knows that thin volume will not boost buying interest."
"The index will linger around 49 points in the next few days with a wait-to-see attitude dominating the market," another broker said.
Eastern Communications was the star on speculative buying in the last few minutes, jumping $0.058 or 7.94 percent to $0.788 on volume of 33,000 shares.
Heilongjiang Electric Power traded the most on inter-institution trading, rising $0.010 or 2.74 percent to $0.374 on volume of 333,800 shares.
Shanghai Vacuum Electron Devices was the biggest loser on expectations of bad results this year, falling $0.006 or 4.61 percent to $0.124 on volume of 278,000 shares.
Shanghai A shares consolidated up later in the session on good market sentiment, brokers said.
The A index rose 1.287 points or 0.14 percent to 907.180 points on volume of 420.4 million shares worth 3.4 billion yuan.
But the SSE 30 index dipped 12.559 points or 0.52 percent to 2386.330 points.
Zhengzhou Baiwen was the star on institutional buying, soaring 0.59 yuan or 10.00 percent to 6.49 yuan on volume of 9.0 million shares.
